teaching.hint: When can two different words finish at the same delimiter?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Two words sharing a delimiter must be in a suffix-containment relation; only distinct words that are not proper suffixes of another need their own block.
solution_outline.approach: Begin with the set of distinct words. Remove every proper suffix of each input word from the set, then sum length plus one delimiter for each survivor.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Survivors are exactly the distinct input words not contained as proper suffixes of any other input word.
solution_outline.correctness: Every removed word is a suffix of a longer word; following that relation terminates at a survivor, so concatenated survivor blocks encode all inputs. Two distinct survivors cannot end at one delimiter, because one would then be a suffix of the other. Each needs at least its own length plus delimiter, giving a lower bound attained by those blocks.
solution_outline.complexity: Expected O(nL²) time for constructing and hashing suffixes, and O(nL) auxiliary space, where L<=7.
solution_outline.pitfall: Prefix or interior-substring sharing does not work: reading continues to the next delimiter.

common_wrong_turns: Prefix or interior-substring sharing does not work: reading continues to the next delimiter.
source_fidelity_notes: Explicitly allowed shared indices and duplicate inputs; preserved next-delimiter reading and length-only output.
